about.description: Richard K. Wolf's path from rock guitar at Oberlin to ethnomusicological fieldwork in South and Central Asia, and the awards, editorships and service that followed.

positions-education-honors.description: Academic positions, education, languages, field research, awards and honors for Richard K. Wolf.

publications.description: Books, edited volumes, articles, reviews and recordings by Richard K. Wolf, many of them available here as offprints.

concepts.description: Conceptual overviews of Richard K. Wolf's work on style, emotion, poetics, space and time, rhythm, and ethnographic creative writing, with links to the writings.

performance.description: Richard K. Wolf on playing the South Indian vīṇā, and recordings of the teachers and students who have performed with him at Harvard.

pedagogy.description: Teaching materials, course listings and student creative work from Richard K. Wolf's courses on music in Islamic contexts, South Asia and Central Asia.

resources.description: Syllabi, handouts, romanisation tables, keyboards, fonts, maps and area studies links gathered for students and researchers of South and Central Asian music.

archives.description: The archives holding Richard K. Wolf's field recordings and videos, where researchers may consult them on site.

bibliographies.description: Bibliographies related to Richard K. Wolf's research, beginning with a bibliography of music in Islam.

dictionaries.description: Online dictionaries of Hindi, Urdu, Panjabi, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Persian and Wakhi that Richard K. Wolf uses in his work, with his own Kota dictionary.

music-of-south-asia-other.description: Indo-Caribbean music in New York, the Nanda Devi festival in Almora, and other South Asian fieldwork outside Richard K. Wolf's main research areas.

research.description: An overview of Richard K. Wolf's ethnomusicological research across India, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Iran, Uzbekistan and Xinjiang, with a way in to each research area.

ritual-daily-life-in-south-india.description: Richard K. Wolf on music in South Indian ritual and daily life, from Kota funerals and god ceremonies to the wider Tamil world around them.

kotas-south-india.description: The Kota tribal people of the Nilgiri Hills: their villages, rituals, god and death repertoires, instruments and songs, with sixteen field videos.

other-nilgiri-groups.description: The Todas, Irulas, Kurumbas, Paniyas and their neighbours in the Nilgiri Hills, and the intertwined musical systems of the plateau and the slopes.

tamil-songs.description: Fieldwork photographs and video of Tamil singers, drummers and lament performers recorded in Tamilnadu between 1982 and 2000.

teyyam.description: Teyyam possession performance in northern Kerala and the Wynad, with chenda drumming and recitation filmed by Richard K. Wolf.

drum-ensembles.description: Drum ensembles of South India, a research area of Richard K. Wolf's still being written.

south-indian-classical-music.description: Richard K. Wolf on Carnatic music, from his first hearing of T. Viswanathan's flute to fieldwork photographs of South Indian classical performance.

music-in-islamic-contexts-in-india-pakis.description: Qawwālī, soz, majlis and Muharram drumming in India and Pakistan, from Richard K. Wolf's fieldwork of 1995 onwards.

music-of-central-asia.description: Fieldwork in Xinjiang, Gilgit-Baltistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and the Wakhan corridor: eighty-eight photographs and seven films of Central Asian musicians.

music-of-iran.description: Photographs and video from Richard K. Wolf's fieldwork in Iran, including zurkhaneh recitation, nauheh, maddh and rowzeh.

laments.description: Lament across Richard K. Wolf's research: Kota āṭḷ, Tamil oppāri and Wakhi funeral song, and the emotional textures of ceremony.

drums-drummers.description: Drums and drummers from Tamilnadu to Panjab, Gilgit and the Caribbean diaspora, in photographs and eight field films.

almora-uttarakhand.description: The Nanda Devi festival and jagaran singing recorded by Richard K. Wolf in Almora, Uttarakhand, in 1998.

indo-caribbean.description: Hosay in Manhattan: Indo-Caribbean tassa drumming and Muharram observance recorded in New York City in 1996.

index.description: Richard K. Wolf, professor of Music and South Asian Studies at Harvard: current ethnographic film projects, fieldwork across South and Central Asia, and a note on how he came to the field.

audiovisual.description: Audio and video examples keyed to Richard K. Wolf's publications: Kota ritual music, Muharram drumming and Sufi dhamali, with two SoundCloud recordings.

portfolio/the-voice-in-the-drum.description: The trailer for The Voice in the Drum: Music, Language and Emotion in Islamicate South Asia, Richard K. Wolf's 2014 book from the University of Illinois Press.

portfolio/sah-na-jai-ho-re-allah.description: Nur Muhammad and Ashakali sing sah na jāī ho re allāh to sarangi accompaniment in Hallaur, Uttar Pradesh, recorded in October 1998.

portfolio/ismoil-nazriev-2.description: Ismoil Nazriev, a Tajik hofiz from Darvoz, in photographs and film made in Dushanbe between 2012 and 2017.

portfolio/wazi_tu_portfolio.description: Daulatsho of Yur, the leading Wakhi poet-singer of Afghanistan, and the making of his song wəzi tu ẓ̌ə jonət tu, in photographs and film.
